issues.description: OTLP LoggingHandler discovered by isinstance scan of root logger handlers instead of held as a reference.
issues.detail: Both _flush_early_log_buffer and _shutdown_telemetry walk logging.getLogger().handlers looking for a LoggingHandler. This couples replay and teardown to global mutable state, breaks if anyone else attaches a LoggingHandler or the SDK refactors, and the two call sites disagree on whether one or many handlers exist. Hold the handler returned by _setup_cloud_tracer and pass it as a value.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler buffer is unbounded with no cap, rotation, or synchronization.
issues.detail: self.buffer is a plain list that grows monotonically for every root-logger record until init_recording or crash. A slow connect, retry storm, or chatty subsystem before session.start() can exhaust memory — a crash-log buffer that itself causes the crash. Use a bounded deque(maxlen=N) or byte cap, state the policy, and log on truncation.

issues.description: Buffer lifecycle is complected across job.py, job_proc_lazy_main.py, and traces.py with no single owner.
issues.detail: Start, stop-without-replay, replay, and drop outcomes are spread across four call sites, and _on_cleanup re-entering init_recording on crash has no documented precondition. No single function names the state machine; the rationale lives only in the PR description. Consolidate ownership in one component and add a literate comment naming the crash-path contract.

issues.description: Unrelated changes folded into the crash-log PR with no justification.
issues.detail: The diff also reorders _queue_msg in worker.py, drops -n auto from unit-tests, silently removes test_plugin_google_stt.py, and adds pythonpath to pyproject. These are CI-time regressions and unrelated mutations with no commit-message audit trail. Split into separate patches so future bisects on log-buffer regressions land on a focused commit.

issues.description: init_recording silently stops buffering on early-return paths, dropping buffered crash logs.
issues.detail: When already initialized or url is non-cloud, init_recording calls _stop_log_buffering with no replay — a mutation hidden behind a guard that reads like a no-op. Buffered records are discarded on a path that looks benign. Pull the stop call above the guard with a comment, or make both outcomes explicit in one named function.

issues.description: Replay and crash paths fail silently when buffered records are lost.
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer's for-loop completes without break if no OTLP handler is found, discarding buffered records with no warning. Likewise _on_cleanup's except path drops records on init_recording failure with no count logged. The whole point of this PR is not losing crash logs — at minimum, count and warn when records are dropped.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR solves a real observability gap — buffer logs early, replay through OTLP on crash — but the implementation is fragile and under-audited. The OTLP handler is discovered by isinstance-scanning the root logger in two places that disagree on cardinality; hold it as a value instead. The buffer is unbounded and could itself cause the crash it's meant to diagnose. Lifecycle is spread across multiple modules with silent-failure paths that drop the very records the feature exists to preserve. Finally, unrelated worker, pytest-xdist, test-file, and pyproject changes are folded in with no audit trail and should be split. Needs-work: bound the buffer, own the handler reference, consolidate the state machine, warn on drops, and split the commit.
